newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Malev plans 1.7 bln forint cargo centre.
newsitem.headline: Malev plans 1.7 bln forint cargo centre.

text.p: BUDAPEST, March 24 (Budapest) - Hungarian national airline Magyar Legikozlekedesi Vallalat (Malev) Rt said on Monday it planned to roughly quadruple its cargo-storage capacity by investing around 1.7 billion forints to open a warehouse at Budapest Ferihegy Airport in the second half of 1998.

"The expected cost is circa 1.7 billion forints," Ferenc Harmath, Malev's commercial manager for cargo operations, told Reuters. "The source of the funds is still an open question -- some of it might come from credit."

The new facility will include 13,000 square meters of usable space, including 8,500 square meters of storage capacity, Harmath said. Malev's storage capacity now is roughly 2,000 square meters, he added.
The other 4,500 square meters in the new facility will include space for 50-to-60 offices for airlines, customs officials, freight forwarders and postal workers, Harmath said.
Malev will abandon its current warehouse, located at Terminal 1, once the new facility opens at Terminal 2, he said.

The airline, which handles cargo for all of the airport's scheduled flights except those of Air France and KLM Royal Dutch Airlines, needs the new storage space to manage growing demand, Harmath said.
"The market will start growing over 20 percent a year starting in 1999," he said. "We need the new cargo facility to handle the additional traffic."
Malev already boosted its cargo handling 10.4 percent to 25,680 tonnes in 1996 from 23,270 tonnes in 1995, Harmath said.

Malev is owned 63.9 percent by the Hungarian State Privatisation and Asset Holding Co (APV Rt), 30.0 percent by Italian airline Alitalia, 5.0 percent by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Trade's investment agency SIMEST and 1.1 percent by other interests, including Hungarian municipalities.
